headline_marked: 11 of 15 [[death sentences handed to Sheikh Hasina and others]] are fugitives
headline: 11 of 15 death sentences handed to Sheikh Hasina and others are fugitives
summary: Out of 61 convicts in crimes against humanity during the July uprising, 40 remain at large, including 11 who received the death penalty.
details: Across six verdicts delivered by the International Crimes Tribunal, 61 individuals have been sentenced. Among them, 15 have been sentenced to death, including ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Of those sentenced to death, 11 are currently fugitives, while only 4 are in custody. This includes Sheikh Hasina, former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan, and former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman.
In addition to the death sentences, 46 others have received various prison terms, including 11 life sentences. Among these, former DIG Syed Nurul Islam has been sentenced to life imprisonment.
The tribunal's chief prosecutor, Md. Aminul Islam, stated that the prosecution has appealed in cases where the sentences were not satisfactory.
The verdicts cover crimes against humanity during the July uprising, as well as disappearances, killings, and torture during the previous Awami League government's tenure.
The first verdict was delivered on November 17, 2024, and the most recent was on June 30. A total of 61 convicts have been sentenced, with 40 fugitives and 21 in custody.

headline: Switzerland lead 1-0 over Algeria at halftime in World Cup clash
summary: The Swiss side holds a narrow advantage as the round-of-32 match continues at BC Place.
details: Switzerland leads Algeria 1-0 at the end of the first half in their World Cup round-of-32 encounter at BC Place.
Both teams made tactical adjustments to their starting lineups for the high-stakes match. Switzerland coach Murat Yakin introduced two changes, while Algeria coach Vladimir Petkovic made three.
For Switzerland, Denis Zakaria stepped in for Luca Jaquez, who was ruled out due to a muscle problem. Winger Dan Ndoye also returned to the starting eleven, replacing midfielder Djibril Sow.

Algeria's changes included Luca Zidane in goal, replacing Oussama Benbot. In defense, Rayan Ait-Nouri replaced Jaouen Hadjam, and Ramiz Zerrouki entered the midfield as Amine Gouiri moved to the bench.
The Swiss lineup featured Gregor Kobel in goal, supported by a defense of Nico Elvedi, Manuel Akanji, and Ricardo Rodriguez.
The Swiss midfield was led by Denis Zakaria, Remo Freuler, Johan Manzambi, and Granit Xhaka, with an attack consisting of Breel Embolo, Dan Ndoye, and Ruben Vargas.
Algeria's squad included Riyad Mahrez and Houssem Aouar, with Luca Zidane guarding the net and a defense featuring Aissa Mandi and Ramy Bensebaini.
caption:
Switzerland takes a 1-0 lead into the break! 🇨🇭
